_meta.purpose: Machine-readable allowlist of INTENTIONAL variance for the janitor's drift checks. See wiki/architecture/fact_inventory.md, recommendation R5 and hazard H1. An entry here declares that a specific difference is DELIBERATE, so the drift detector suppresses it and the intentional difference never reads as a bug.
_meta.why_this_file_exists: H1: 'Intentional variance must be encoded as machine-readable data next to the code, never as prose in an audit. Until that encoding exists, [the drift table] is an attractive nuisance.' This file is that encoding. Prose comments (e.g. build_bundle.py's 'MacIntyre is the book's author') explain intent to humans but are invisible to the detector; this file makes the same intent executable.
rules: Add an entry ONLY for deliberate variance that has a recorded rationale. NEVER silence a real drift bug here just to quiet the report.
Every entry needs 'reason' (why the difference is intentional) and 'source' (where the intent is authoritatively recorded in code or docs).

A hex MISMATCH -- the same tradition assigned two different colors by two pipelines -- is never allowlistable. That is always a hand-copy bug. Only ABSENCES (a tradition deliberately omitted from a pipeline) belong here.

palette_absence.reason: MacIntyre is the book's AUTHOR, not a satellite tradition. commentary-explorer/build_bundle.py deliberately excludes him because he has no satellite page (the text being annotated is his); his absence from that pipeline's palette is correct, not drift.
